related_questions.question: Can I check my immigration status online?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can check the status of most U.S. immigration applications online through USCIS Case Status Online. To do this, you will need your receipt number, which is a 13-character identifier (three letters followed by 10 numbers) provided on the receipt notice for your application.
How to check your immigration status online:

list.snippet: Locate your receipt number: This number is found on the receipt notice you received from USCIS after submitting your application.
Go to the USCIS Case Status Online tool: Navigate to the USCIS Case Status Online page.
Enter your receipt number: Input your receipt number into the designated field.
Check the status: Click the "Check Status" button to view the current status of your case.

related_questions.question: What is the 7 year rule for immigrants?

text_blocks.snippet: The term "7-year rule" for immigrants doesn't refer to a single, universally applicable law, but rather to a potential pathway to a green card through the Registry program, which is being updated by current legislation. This bill, called the "Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929," proposes a rolling registry date, allowing individuals to apply for registry after residing in the United States for at least seven years.
snippet_highlighted_words: a potential pathway to a green card through the Registry program

list.title: Existing Registry Program:
list.snippet: The current registry program allows certain non-U.S. nationals who entered the U.S. before January 1, 1972, to apply for a green card.

list.title: Proposed Change:
list.snippet: The bill would remove the specific 1972 cutoff date and instead allow those who have resided in the U.S. for at least seven years to apply for registry.

list.title: Who is eligible?
list.snippet: This bill, if passed, would make a green card pathway available to millions of long-term U.S. residents, including those who entered without authorization and have lived in the U.S. for many years.

list.title: Key Requirement:
list.snippet: The main requirement for this pathway is continuous residence in the United States for at least seven years.

list.title: "Continuous Residence":
list.snippet: This means maintaining a permanent dwelling place in the U.S. over the required period, which is generally the applicant's actual physical location.

list.title: Impact:
list.snippet: This legislation could have a significant impact on the lives of many immigrants who have been contributing to the U.S. for decades, providing them with a pathway to legal permanent residency and eventual citizenship, according to the American Immigration Council.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that this is a proposed change to immigration law, and the bill is still under consideration in Congress.

related_questions.question: How to check USCIS online account number?

text_blocks.snippet: To find your USCIS online account number, log in to your USCIS online account and navigate to your profile or account settings. The number is typically located there. If you previously filed a paper form, you may have received an "USCIS Online Account Access Notice" with the number, usually on a receipt notice from USCIS.
snippet_highlighted_words: log in to your USCIS online account and navigate to your profile or account settings

list.title: 1. Log in to your USCIS online account:
list.snippet: Go to the USCIS website and access your account.
Profile/Account Settings: Once logged in, find the "Profile" or "Account Settings" section within your account.
Receipt Notice: If you previously filed a paper form, check your receipt notice (Form I-797C, Notice of Action) for the "USCIS Online Account Access Notice".

list.title: 3. Alternative:
list.snippet: If you can't find it, you can also check your case status online using your receipt number on the USCIS website.

list.title: 4. Online Access Code:
list.snippet: If you filed online, you will be issued an Online Access Code (OAC), which you can find on your account dashboard or profile.

list.title: 5. Request a new code:
list.snippet: If you have lost the online access code or it has expired, you can request a new one via USCIS online portal.
